body:
Tested and it makes the option work great with RenderDoc. However, it's worth noting that `--generate-spirv-debug-info` is listed as a debug feature in the documentation, `Available in editor builds and debug export templates only`, but these changes make it work in exported release projects too.

It probably shouldn't be allowed since we don't want published games to be able to generate debugging info. Maybe make it work only if the release template was built with `debug_symbols=yes`.

> However, it's worth noting that `--generate-spirv-debug-info` is listed as a debug feature in the documentation, `Available in editor builds and debug export templates only`, but these changes make it work in exported release projects too.

The command-line option doesn't seem to be excluded from release builds or non-editor builds, and there's a lot of ifdefs around them with DEBUG_ENABLED, so it seems pretty explicit that it's included. It sounds like a documentation error.

What I'm thinking is that the exporter just shouldn't allow to use the shader baking option if the editor was run with this feature.

> What I'm thinking is that the exporter just shouldn't allow to use the shader baking option if the editor was run with this feature.

Wouldn't it defeat your point in my PR that the editor should be able to export a project independently from editor specifics? We are debugging the editor itself when running it with this option, so it shouldn't affect the run instance or exported project.

> Wouldn't it defeat your point in my PR that the editor should be able to export a project independently from editor specifics? We are debugging the editor itself when running it with this option, so it shouldn't affect the run instance or exported project.

No, shader baker is definitely affected by this setting because the shader creation runs on the editor itself, which is being run with this setting. We need to block the shader baker from being used if the commandline option is being used.

When I test this with an existing project it fails to compile any shaders. ~I am assuming users will need to manually clear the shader cache? Perhaps we need to increment the shader version number or something to break the cache automatically~

_Edit: clearing cache doesn't help. With this PR and `--generate-spirv-debug-info` it seems like no shaders can compile_

_Edit: edit: It seems like my device just doesnt support `--generate-spirv-debug-info` :/ it fails with 4.4.1 too_

Added the warning.

I'm unable to detect a way to fix @clayjohn's error. The extension doesn't make any API changes, and the extension is also requested as required if the command line option is enabled. This seems like a driver error. The opcode in question that is mentioned in the error is very standard and the extension shouldn't be affecting its usage, as the Phi operator is essential for any code that involves branching.

Regardless of what we might explore on how to solve this, this is a direct regression fix for something currently present in `master` so I don't think we should have much concern for merging this. What we do want to explore is some alternate way to offer the ability to not strip the debug information when smolv is used without affecting the shader cache hashes if possible. But I don't think we should block this PR and we can evaluate that later.
